docs.title: Magic items of the Ember Company
Lantern of the Drowned
docs.text:
Wondrous item, uncommon

While lit, this green-glass lantern sheds dim light in a 20-foot radius. Undead within the light can't hide, and you know the direction of the nearest undead within 1 mile. The lantern burns for 1 hour per day.

docs.title: Tess's Weighted Purse
docs.text:
Wondrous item, common

This purse always feels slightly heavier than it should. Once per day, when you search it, you find 1d4 copper pieces that weren't there before. Nobody knows whose they are.

docs.title: Game rules
docs.text: The house rules currently in effect. Older versions are gone for good.

docs.title: Potions
docs.text: Drinking any potion is a bonus action. If you use your action instead, a healing potion heals its maximum.

docs.title: One spell slot per turn
docs.text: You can spend at most one spell slot per turn, reaction included. Spells cast without a slot (racial traits, items, scrolls) don't count toward this limit.

docs.title: Critical hits
docs.text:
On a critical hit, roll the extra damage dice normally and add the maximum of one die.

Changing a rule

Rule changes are proposed at the end of a session and voted on by the whole table.

docs.title: Table rules
docs.text: How we play together, out of character.

docs.title: Safe word
docs.text: If you are uncomfortable or need to step out of the game, say LIGHTHOUSE. No questions asked, we pause or move on.

docs.title: Dice
docs.text: A die that falls off the table or lands cocked gets rerolled.

docs.title: Missing players
docs.text: If two players (or the DM) can't make it, the session is skipped. If one player is missing, we play a one-shot with pre-generated characters.

docs.title: Snacks
docs.text: Whoever hosts provides drinks. Everyone else brings snacks.

docs.title: Session 0
docs.text:
Thaw 1, 512 AC · played on 2026-01-10 · Party EMBER

Our heroes meet on the deck of a leaking fishing boat bound for Greywater. Mira, human fighter and former city guard. Dorn, dwarf cleric of the forge. Tess, halfling rogue with a suspiciously heavy purse. The captain swears the fog is ordinary. It is not.

On the beach, drowned sailors rise from the surf. The party survives, barely, and climbs to the village on the cliffs, where Elder Hanne offers shelter in exchange for answers: why have the dead stopped resting?

docs.title: The Ambush at Greywater Pass
docs.text:
Thaw 3, 512 AC · played on 2026-01-24 · Party TIDE

A hundred miles inland, a second group is hired to escort a salt caravan to the coast. Kael, elf wizard who reads too much. Rook, half-orc barbarian who reads too little. Isa, tiefling bard who reads people.

At Greywater Pass the caravan is ambushed by bandits wearing the gull sigil of the Saltbrokers' Guild, the very guild that hired them. Rook wins the fight. Isa wins the interrogation. Kael finds the map in the bandit leader's boot: an X on the cliffs above Greywater village.

docs.title: Two Fires on the Cliff
docs.text:
Thaw 6, 512 AC · played on 2026-02-07 · Party EMBER, TIDE

The two parties meet for the first time, swords drawn, on the cliff marked on Kael's map. The Ember Company thinks the strangers raised the dead. The Tidebound think the strangers work for the Guild. Tess and Isa, both reaching for the same purse, are the first to start laughing.

Comparing notes around two campfires, they piece it together: since the ambush at the pass, the Guild has been shipping something up the coast inside the salt barrels, and wherever the barrels go, the dead follow.

docs.title: The Saltbrokers' Ledger
docs.text:
Bloom 14, 512 AC · played on 2026-03-07 · Party TIDE

Months later, the Tidebound infiltrate the Guild's counting house in the capital. Isa talks her way past the clerks, Kael copies the ledger page by page, and Rook stands very still in a corridor pretending to be a statue, which works far better than anyone expected.

The ledger names a buyer for the barrels: someone signing only as the Tidekeeper.
